Container counts come from the nursery plant list. A lower “marked for sale” figure means some of those containers are not flagged for sale. Stock plants are counted beside the colour, not inside it. Indoor marks a plant that can live in a room, including on a sunny windowsill. Sun, semi-shade and shade follow that same list. Where the light field was blank, or a mark disagreed with cultivation advice for Melbourne, it was checked against the Australian Native Plants Society, the Australian National Botanic Gardens, PlantZAfrica, the Missouri Botanical Garden and the Royal Horticultural Society. Drought tolerant means the plant handles a dry spell once it is established. The bottle mark means the flowers are fragrant. Aromatic leaves are left unmarked. Tank bromeliads are left unmarked, because the leaf cup still needs water. Endangered and Vulnerable are Victoria’s Flora and Fauna Guarantee Act listings, from the FFG Threatened List of July 2026, and apply only where that list names the plant. Each listing sits under that plant’s picture. Photos are included where this project already has a checked picture, or where Wikimedia Commons has a file titled with that plant’s name. 391 of 676 plants have a photo.
